Til, First-borne.''] {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=Tradition.}}Heluidius of old abused these wordes, ''til'', and, ''first-borne'', agaynst the perpetual virginity of our B. Ladie. ''Hiero. cont. Helu''. Which truth though not expressed in Scripture, yet our Aduersaries also do graunt, and Heluidius for denial therof was condemned for an heretike by tradition only. ''Aug. hær.84''.

{{c|{{larger|{{sc|Chap. II.}}}}}}

{{c|''The Gentils come vnto Christ with their offerings. and that so openly, that the Iewes can not pretend ignorance. 3 The Iewes with Herode conspire against him. 13 He therevpon fleeth from them into Aegypt. 16 They afterward, seing their subteltie preuailed not, imagined to oppresse him by open persecution. 19 But they at length dyed, and he returneth to the land of Israel: al according to the Scriptures.''}} {{verse|chapter=2|verse=1}}{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=The holy feast of the ''Epiphanie'' called ''Twelfth-day'' the 6 of Ianuarie. vpon which day this is the Gospel.}}WHEN IESVS therfore vvas {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Luc. 2, 7.''}}* borne in Bethlehem of Iuda in the dayes of Herod the King, ‖ behold, there came Sages from the East to Hierusalem, {{verse|chapter=2|verse=2}}† saying, vvhere is he that is borne King of the Ievves? For vve haue seene his ‖ starre in the East, and ‖ are come to adore him. {{verse|chapter=2|verse=3}}† And Herod the King hearing this, vvas troubled, & al Hierusalem vvith him. {{verse|chapter=2|verse=4}}† And assembling together al the high Priestes & the Scribes of the people, he ‖ inquired of them vvhere Christ should be borne. {{verse|chapter=2|verse=5}}† But they sayd to him, In Bethlehē of Iuda. For so it is vvritten by the Prophet: {{verse|chapter=2|verse=6}}† ''And thou Bethlehem the land of Iuda, art not the least among the Princes of Iuda: for out of thee shal come forth the Capitaine that shal rule my people Israel''.{{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Mich. 5, 2.''}} {{verse|chapter=2|verse=7}}† Then Herod secretly calling the Sages, learned diligently of them the time of the starre which appeared to them: {{verse|chapter=2|verse=8}}† and sending them into Bethlehem, sayd, Goe, and inquire diligently of the childe: and when you shal finde him, make reporte to me, that I also may come and adore him.

{{verse|chapter=2|verse=9}}† Who hauing heard the king, went their way: and behold the starre which they had seen in the East, went before them, vntil it came & stoode ouer, where the childe was. {{verse|chapter=2|verse=10}}† And seing the starre, they reioyced vvith exceding great ioy. {{verse|chapter=2|verse=11}}† And entring into the house, they found the childe vvith MARIE his mother, & falling dovvne ‖ adored him: and opening their ‖ treasures, they offered to him {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Psa. 71, 10.''}}* ‖ giftes: gold, frankincense, & myrrhe. {{verse|chapter=2|verse=12}}† And hauing receiued an ansvver in sleepe that they should not returne to Herod, they vvent backe an other vvay into their countrey.⊣

{{verse|chapter=2|verse=13}}† {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=The Gospel of ''Childermas'' day.}}And after they vvere departed, behold an Angel of our Lord appeared in sleepe to Ioseph, saying: Arise, & take the childe & his mother, & flee into Aegypt: and be there vntil I shal tel the. For it wil come to passe that Herod vvil seeke the childe to destroy him. {{verse|chapter=2|verse=14}}† Who arose, & tooke the childe<noinclude>{{rh||A iij|and}}</noinclude>
